units.title: How to read the Bible
units.eq: How does God speak in Scripture?

lessons.title: God’s word in human words
lessons.idea: God is the author of Scripture; human authors wrote in their own style and time. Both truths matter.
lessons.question: If God is the author, why do the books differ in style?
lessons.activity: Compare two accounts of the same event (e.g., the Gospels of Matthew and Mark) and list differences and agreements.

lessons.title: Literary forms and the senses of Scripture
lessons.idea: Scripture uses history, poetry, law and prophecy. The Church reads it for its literal and spiritual senses.
lessons.question: What is the difference between literal and spiritual senses?
lessons.activity: Match texts with literary forms; read Genesis 1 as poetry.

lessons.title: Scripture, Tradition and the Magisterium
lessons.idea: The Church reads Scripture within living Tradition, guided by the Magisterium.
lessons.question: Why do Catholics rely on Tradition as well as the Bible?
lessons.activity: Make a three-legged stool diagram and explain it.

lessons.title: Creation: a gift
lessons.idea: God created the world good. Humans are the summit of creation.
lessons.question: What does Genesis 1 teach?
lessons.activity: Read Genesis 1 and identify its theological claims.

lessons.title: The fall
lessons.idea: Sin entered the world through Adam and Eve. All suffer its effects.
lessons.question: How does sin spread?
lessons.activity: Study the three questions: what, how, why.

lessons.title: Cain and Abel; Noah; Babel
lessons.idea: Sin grows, but God keeps his promise. He saves a remnant.
lessons.question: What do these stories show?
lessons.activity: Create a timeline of the first eleven chapters.

units.title: The patriarchs
units.eq: How does God choose a people?

lessons.title: Abraham: father of faith
lessons.idea: God calls Abraham and promises him descendants and land.
lessons.question: Why is Abraham our father in faith?
lessons.activity: Retell Abraham’s journey on a map.

lessons.title: Isaac and Jacob
lessons.idea: God’s promise passes on. Jacob wrestles with God.
lessons.question: What does Jacob’s new name mean?
lessons.activity: Compare the lives of the patriarchs.

lessons.title: Joseph: from slavery to rescue
lessons.idea: God turns evil into good.
lessons.question: How does Joseph forgive?
lessons.activity: Role-play Genesis 45.

units.title: Exodus and the Law
units.eq: How does God save and teach?

lessons.title: The call of Moses
lessons.idea: God hears the cry of his people. He calls Moses.
lessons.question: How does God reveal his name?
lessons.activity: Study “I AM WHO I AM.”

lessons.title: Passover and the Red Sea
lessons.idea: God frees Israel. The Passover points to Christ.
lessons.question: How does Passover foreshadow Easter?
lessons.activity: Compare Passover and the Last Supper.

lessons.title: Sinai: the Law and covenant
lessons.idea: God gives the Law to form his people.
lessons.question: How are the Ten Commandments a gift?
lessons.activity: Rank the Commandments by theme.

units.title: Kings and prophets
units.eq: How does God lead his people?

lessons.title: Samuel, Saul and David
lessons.idea: Israel asks for a king. God chooses David.
lessons.question: What did God promise David?
lessons.activity: Draw a family tree from David to Jesus.

lessons.title: Solomon and the Temple
lessons.idea: Solomon builds the Temple. It is the house of God.
lessons.question: Why is the Temple important?
lessons.activity: Build a model of the Temple.

lessons.title: The prophets
lessons.idea: Prophets call Israel back to God and foretell the Messiah.
lessons.question: What is a prophet’s job?
lessons.activity: Read an Isaiah passage and Gospel fulfillment.

lessons.title: The exile
lessons.idea: Israel is taken to Babylon. God does not abandon them.
lessons.question: What hope does Jeremiah give?
lessons.activity: Write a letter from an exile.

lessons.title: Restoration
lessons.idea: God brings his people home. They rebuild the Temple.
lessons.question: How does the community renew?
lessons.activity: Look at the timeline of return.

lessons.title: The Psalms and Wisdom
lessons.idea: Israel prays and seeks wisdom.
lessons.question: Which psalm resonates?
lessons.activity: Write your own psalm.

units.title: Preparing for the Messiah
units.eq: How did the Old Testament point to Christ?

lessons.title: The promises of the Messiah
lessons.idea: The prophets foretell a coming king and servant.
lessons.question: Which prophecies are fulfilled?
lessons.activity: Create a chart of prophecies and fulfillment.

lessons.title: Types of Christ
lessons.idea: Moses, David and the manna foreshadow Jesus.
lessons.question: What is a type?
lessons.activity: Match types with fulfillments.

lessons.title: The Old Testament in the liturgy
lessons.idea: We hear and pray the Old Testament at Mass.
lessons.question: Which readings do you remember?
lessons.activity: Look at this Sunday’s first reading.

units.title: Living the Old Testament faith today

lessons.title: The Ten Commandments for today
lessons.idea: The Commandments show how to love.
lessons.question: How do they apply now?
lessons.activity: Debate scenarios.

lessons.title: Justice and mercy
lessons.idea: The prophets defend the poor.
lessons.question: What does God require?
lessons.activity: Create a justice project.

lessons.title: Prayer with the psalms
lessons.idea: The Psalms are the Church’s prayer book.
lessons.question: Which psalm do you use?
lessons.activity: Practice lectio divina with a psalm.
